summary: Iteration 15 validated the reworked company flow end-to-end: 5-free-then-₹29 unlocks, ₹1,99,000/yr subscription (mock payments), banner editor + home-page listing, Standard CV PDF download (subscribed + 20/day), and EditPostDialog persisting vessel_name/port/audits. 7/8 backend tests pass; 1 documented backend bug (provider_card omits new fields to seekers). All requested frontend flows pass; one minor state-refresh issue (Download CV button appears only after page reload post-subscribe).

minor.issue: provider_card() at server.py:628 does not include vessel_name / port / audits. PUT /provider/requirement correctly persists them and company-side /matches['requirement'] echoes them, but seekers never see these new fields on their match cards — contradicts the review-request contract 'GET /api/matches returns them'.

integration_issues.issue: After clicking subscribe-btn and CompanyPlan flips to active, the Matches component's local `status` state is not re-fetched. The download-cv-<id> button (gated on status?.subscribed) only appears after a full page reload. First testing attempt failed with an 8s wait for download-cv-<SID>; API state was correct.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py provider_card() must include vessel_name, port and audits so seekers can actually see them in /matches and /browse — otherwise EditPostDialog changes are invisible to crew.
Home page 'How it works' step 04 still references ₹49 unlock and ₹499 boost. Not part of updated review copy — should read '5 free unlocks then ₹29' (and align with the new ₹1,99,000/yr plan).

CompanyPlan.subscribe() only refreshes /company/status; sibling Matches component keeps stale `status.subscribed=false`, so the Download CV button (and the 'Unlock free' unlimited label) only appears after a manual page reload. Consider lifting `status` to a shared store, emitting an event on subscribe, or re-fetching on tab focus.

Audit date input in EditPostDialog appears to save the value verbatim (observed '20/26/0420' from a 2026-04-20 <input type=date>). The frontend is probably mis-formatting DD/MM/YYYY vs YYYY-MM-DD before posting. Backend accepts it as an opaque string, so review request's {type,date} shape ends up polluted. Recommend either standardising to YYYY-MM-DD or parsing before save.
server.py is 1,899 lines — well above the 700-line guideline; consider splitting into routers (auth, seeker, provider, pay, company, matches, alerts, referral).

test_credentials.md still documents old pricing (₹49 unlock, ₹499 boost, ₹100 registration) and should be updated to reflect the new company flow so the next testing agent starts from the correct baseline.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable regression: /app/backend/tests/test_company_flow_v2.py (run with `pytest -o addopts= backend/tests/test_company_flow_v2.py`). Key gotchas: (1) /matches response uses 'matches' key, not 'results'; (2) redacted contacts render as '🔒 Locked' (with lock emoji + space), not plain 'Locked'; (3) mock Razorpay is triggered whenever RAZORPAY_KEY_ID/SECRET are unset in backend/.env — order_id starts with 'order_mock_'; (4) provider_card currently omits vessel_name/port/audits — will need a re-run after main-agent fix. Home page banners are cumulative across runs (5 present in the dev DB) — assertions should use >=1 rather than an exact count.
rca of the issue: Seekers can't see vessel_name/port/audits because /matches builds provider cards via provider_card() (server.py:628) which whitelists only the legacy fields — the new columns from ProviderRequirement (added at lines 188-190) are silently dropped even though PUT persists them and matches_requirement() sees them. Fix: extend provider_card()'s dict with `'vessel_name': p.get('vessel_name',''), 'port': p.get('port',''), 'audits': p.get('audits') or []` (or splat `**{k: p.get(k) for k in ('vessel_name','port','audits')}`).
